entries.description: Refused to write 256 into the Lean. A numeral would have baked Q8.8 into the file and made it the first of 224 hardware theorem signatures to pin a format — undoing corpus-wide the property that made this whole step cheap.

Halted the regime-simplification bridge and stated the obstruction as a lemma-shaped claim: it needs multiplicative cancellation, and le_of_mul_le_mul_left / mul_pos / one_div_pos_of_pos are all unreachable from this import root. Re-deriving three ordered-field lemmas to save callers one arithmetic step is the wrong trade.

Wrote into the FILE, not just the commit, that hinv0 is measured rather than proved and that the Q8.8 bound is no stronger than a bench measurement. A caveat that lives only in a commit message is a caveat nobody re-reads.

findings.description: Q8.8 assembly shipped: nr_reciprocal_2stage_at_format + quantum_nonneg, numeral-free so the format stays an input. The chip's proof debt is discharged — hs proved, hreg is call-site arithmetic, hinv0 carried as a hypothesis with the measured 7.57x seed margin attached. 575/575, sorryAx-free, AxiomLedger unchanged.

Two independent instruments agree on which envelope dominates at Q8.8: the PROOF's regime admits |b|<=62.5 while the MEASURED usable domain is |b| in [0.125,16). Representability binds first, not the regime — the same conclusion the RTL header reaches for Q16.16 by a different route.
